clue.text: Fruit's pungent - one could get peppered with it

definitions.text: one could get peppered with it

blocks.note: a grape is a fruit, plus the possessive S
pungent, spicy food is hot

explanation.surface: A tasting note on a sharp-flavoured fruit, followed by a warning about something that sprays you.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash separates wordplay from definition; 'peppered' hints at spice but means riddled with shot.
explanation.definitionFit: Grapeshot was a cannon load of small iron balls that peppered, or riddled, its targets with many hits.

clue.text: Got the shakes in run-down part of town

indicators.note: to shake something is to jumble it about, so these letters get rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone became nervous while walking through a seedy neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghetto is a poor, deprived and often crowded district of a city.

clue.text: A bishop posted elsewhere

blocks.note: taken as written
B is the chess notation for bishop
a letter that is posted has been sent

explanation.surface: A clergyman has been transferred to another diocese.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone absent is not present, being somewhere else instead, so the adjective matches elsewhere used predicatively.

clue.text: Every single one kept in by schoolteacher

indicators.note: what is kept in by something sits inside it, so the answer lies within the following word

blocks.note: the letters sit inside this word, after SCHOOLT

explanation.surface: Every pupil in the class was given detention by the teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Each refers to every one of a group taken individually, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Compassion shown by family after interval in play

indicators.note: after says one piece comes behind another, so the family follows the interval in the answer

blocks.note: to have heart is to show compassion
an interval is a break
a house is a family line, as in the House of Windsor

explanation.surface: A theatre review praising the warmth shown by a stage family in the second half.
explanation.walkthrough: 'family' means a dynastic line here, as in a royal house, not the people on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartbreak House is a 1919 play by George Bernard Shaw, so it is an example of a play.

clue.text: Ignored what Nelson did?

blocks.note: first meaning: deliberately overlooked something
second meaning, literal: at Copenhagen in 1801 Nelson put his telescope to his blind eye to avoid seeing a signal

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second meaning as a literal account of a historical anecdote; Admiral Nelson had lost the sight of one eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for deliberately overlooking wrongdoing comes from Nelson pretending not to see an order to withdraw.

clue.text: Fellow drinking last of Soave, good value

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept
someone drinking takes something inside, so one piece goes into the other

blocks.note: a chap is a fellow
the final letter of Soave

explanation.surface: A man sipping an Italian white wine remarks that it is a bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: Soave is a dry white wine from the Veneto in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cheap costs little, so it represents good value for money.

clue.text: Critic he upset going round cold Welsh resort

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and disordered, so these letters are rearranged
going round something means surrounding it, so the jumble wraps the other piece

blocks.note: taken as written
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A reviewer is annoyed at having to circle a chilly seaside town in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Criccieth is a small seaside town with a castle on the Llŷn Peninsula in north-west Wales.

clue.text: Skipping rope kept in fancy tent in warehouse

indicators.note: skipping suggests jumping about, so the letters of the first word are scrambled
fancy means elaborate or reworked, so the letters of the second word are rearranged too
what is kept in something is held inside it, so one jumble sits within the other

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A child's skipping rope is stored inside a decorative tent in a storehouse.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrepôt is a trading port or depot where goods are stored before re-export, hence a warehouse.

clue.text: Headway made by pair chased by wicked witch

indicators.note: what is chased by something has that thing coming after it, fixing the order of the parts

blocks.note: PR is the abbreviation for pair
an ogress is a cruel, frightening woman, as a wicked witch is

explanation.surface: Two characters fleeing a witch, as in a fairy tale, are getting somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Progress is forward movement towards a goal, which is what making headway means.

clue.text: The sort of seat that may suit a lazy professor?

definitions.text: The sort of seat that may suit a lazy professor?

blocks.note: surface reading: a comfortable armchair for lounging
setter's reading: a professor holds an academic chair, and an idle one would want an undemanding post

explanation.walkthrough: A university professorship is called a chair, so the answer is both a soft armchair and an untaxing appointment.
explanation.definitionFit: An easy chair is a large, comfortable upholstered armchair, and literally an undemanding professorship.

clue.text: Start of number trio's playing?

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, so only that letter is taken
musicians playing move about freely, so these letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: the opening letter of number
taken as written; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A musical threesome begins performing a song.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition doubles as part of the wordplay: its first letter joins the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is the opening passage of a song, and a song is a number in musical slang.

clue.text: Look after a number accompanied by daughter

blocks.note: ten is a number
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A parent cares for a group of children along with a daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: To tend someone is to care for them, as a nurse tends a patient.

clue.text: Avoid bullock? Sure

blocks.note: a steer is a young castrated bull, a bullock
to be clear about something is to be sure of it

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to keep away from a young bull, and is told yes.
explanation.definitionFit: To steer clear of something is the idiom for keeping well away from it.

clue.text: More than one Dalmatian follows behind coach

definitions.text: More than one Dalmatian follows behind coach

blocks.clueFragment: More than one Dalmatian follows behind coach
blocks.note: surface reading: a sports team's mascot trailing the trainer
setter's reading: a horse-drawn coach, which spotted dogs were bred to run behind

explanation.walkthrough: 'coach' suggests a trainer; Dalmatians were historically trained to trot beside and behind horse-drawn coaches as guards.
explanation.definitionFit: Dalmatians were known as carriage dogs because they escorted horse-drawn carriages.

clue.text: Royal Navy chaps put in a spot of decking

indicators.note: what is put in something is placed inside it, so one group goes within the other

blocks.note: RN is the abbreviation for Royal Navy
chaps are men
a dot is a spot

explanation.surface: Sailors are set down on a patch of a ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decking' looks like ship's planking, but it is the verb deck, to decorate.
explanation.definitionFit: Decking in the sense of decorating, as in decking the halls, is adornment, an ornamental addition.

clue.text: Object of loathing and hate a man exploited

indicators.note: something exploited is worked over and manipulated, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone loathed and hated a man who took advantage of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Anathema is something or someone intensely detested, as in 'the idea was anathema to her'.

clue.text: Odd having left in choke

indicators.note: to have something is to hold it, so one piece is held within the other

blocks.note: odd means strange
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Someone feels oddly choked up after walking out.
explanation.definitionFit: To strangle someone is to choke them by squeezing the throat.

clue.text: In a lot at a French hotel in resort? No way!

annotation.answer: NOT FOR ALL THE TEA IN CHINA

indicators.note: to re-sort is to sort again, so the preceding letters are put into a new order

blocks.clueFragment: In a lot at a French hotel in
blocks.note: taken as written, every letter used

explanation.surface: Someone refuses outright to stay at a French hotel at a holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' reads as a holiday destination, but is re-sort, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'not for all the tea in China' means not at any price, an emphatic refusal.

clue.text: Brave, old man in pain?

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: pa, or old man, is a father
an ache is a pain

explanation.surface: A question of whether an elderly man is being courageous about his suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brave' looks like an adjective, but it is the noun for a Native American warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: A brave is a Native American warrior, and an Apache is a member of one such people.

clue.text: Composer in carriage in capital city

blocks.note: first meaning: Irving ..., the American songwriter
second meaning: a four-wheeled covered carriage
third meaning: the capital of Germany

explanation.walkthrough: A triple definition: the composer, a type of carriage named after the city, and the city itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Irving Berlin wrote White Christmas, a berlin is a kind of coach, and Berlin is Germany's capital.

clue.text: See 17
Primate burying Saint in recess of church

indicators.note: to bury something is to put it inside, so one piece is enclosed by the other

blocks.note: an ape is a primate
S is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: An archbishop buries a saint in an alcove of the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' suggests an archbishop, which suits the church setting, but here it is the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is the semicircular vaulted recess at the end of a church, usually behind the altar.

clue.text: Former politician may be hot wearing toupee

indicators.note: something worn is covered by the item worn, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for hot
a toupee is a small wig

explanation.surface: An old-time statesman sweats under his hairpiece.
explanation.definitionFit: The Whigs were a British political party that later became the Liberals, so a Whig is a politician of the past.

clue.text: Hunting dog dropping black bird

indicators.note: dropping something means letting it go, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: a beagle is a hound used for hunting hares
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A hound lets go of a blackbird it caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'black bird' looks like the blackbird; 'black' belongs with the deletion and 'bird' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagle is a large bird of prey, so it is an example of a bird.

clue.text: Shady, until each reformed

indicators.note: something reformed is formed again in a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Dubious characters, until every one of them turned over a new leaf.
explanation.definitionFit: Shady dealings are disreputable or dishonest, which is what unethical describes.

clue.text: Prevent a check pinning rook

indicators.note: pinning something holds it fast within, so one piece is trapped inside the other

blocks.note: to vet is to check
R is the chess notation for rook

explanation.surface: A chess move: a check that pins the opponent's rook stops their plan.
explanation.definitionFit: To avert something is to ward it off, so it is a synonym of prevent.

clue.text: Holly, say, always jealous

blocks.note: ever means always, as in forever
green with envy, so jealous

explanation.surface: Someone called Holly is forever envious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holly' reads as a woman's name, but it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Holly keeps its leaves all year round, making it an example of an evergreen plant.
